note: Frozen task corpus for the LMPL 2026 pilot. 24 tasks, 6 strata x 4. Contracts are language neutral. Interface boilerplate is language specific. Expected outputs are generated from the two reference implementations, which must agree on every case before any model run.

tasks.contract: Write a function that clamps an integer n into the closed range [lo, hi]. If n is below lo return lo. If n is above hi return hi. Otherwise return n. The caller guarantees lo <= hi.
tasks.sig_L: function clamp(n: int, lo: int, hi: int) -> int
tasks.sig_py: def clamp(n: int, lo: int, hi: int) -> int

tasks.contract: Write a function that returns the Manhattan distance between points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2), that is the sum of the absolute coordinate differences.
tasks.sig_L: function dist(x1: int, y1: int, x2: int, y2: int) -> int
tasks.sig_py: def dist(x1: int, y1: int, x2: int, y2: int) -> int

tasks.contract: Write a function that scales a rectangle record with integer fields w and h by an integer factor k, returning a new record with both fields multiplied by k.
tasks.sig_L: function scale(r: { w: int, h: int }, k: int) -> { w: int, h: int }
tasks.sig_py: def scale(r: Rect, k: int) -> Rect  (Rect is a provided dataclass with int fields w, h)

tasks.contract: Write a function that labels a Gregorian year. Return the string leap when the year is a leap year and the string common otherwise. A year is a leap year when it is divisible by 4, except that century years are leap years only when divisible by 400. Years are positive.
tasks.sig_L: function leapLabel(y: int) -> string
tasks.sig_py: def leap_label(y: int) -> str

tasks.contract: Write a function that returns the sum of the even values in an integer array. The empty array sums to 0. All values are non-negative.
tasks.sig_L: function sumEvens(xs: Array<int>) -> int
tasks.sig_py: def sum_evens(xs: list[int]) -> int

tasks.contract: Write a function that counts how many values in an integer array are strictly greater than a threshold t.
tasks.sig_L: function countAbove(xs: Array<int>, t: int) -> int
tasks.sig_py: def count_above(xs: list[int], t: int) -> int

tasks.contract: Write a function that returns the largest value in a non-empty integer array.
tasks.sig_L: function maxOf(xs: Array<int>) -> int
tasks.sig_py: def max_of(xs: list[int]) -> int

tasks.contract: Write a function that returns the dot product of two integer arrays of equal length. Two empty arrays give 0.
tasks.sig_L: function dot(xs: Array<int>, ys: Array<int>) -> int
tasks.sig_py: def dot(xs: list[int], ys: list[int]) -> int

tasks.contract: Write a function that converts a score from 0 to 100 into a letter grade string. 90 and above is A, 80 to 89 is B, 70 to 79 is C, 60 to 69 is D, anything lower is F.
tasks.sig_L: function grade(score: int) -> string
tasks.sig_py: def grade(score: int) -> str

tasks.contract: Write a function for one fizzbuzz value. For a positive integer n return fizzbuzz when n is divisible by both 3 and 5, fizz when divisible by 3 only, buzz when divisible by 5 only, and otherwise the decimal digits of n as a string.
tasks.sig_L: function fizz(n: int) -> string
tasks.sig_py: def fizz(n: int) -> str

tasks.contract: Write a function that moves a point one step on a grid. Direction N increases y by 1, S decreases y by 1, E increases x by 1, W decreases x by 1, and any other direction string leaves the point unchanged. Return the resulting point.
tasks.sig_L: function move(dir: string, x: int, y: int) -> { x: int, y: int }
tasks.sig_py: def move(dir: str, x: int, y: int) -> Point  (Point is a provided dataclass with int fields x, y)

tasks.contract: Write a function computing a stylized tax in whole units from a non-negative integer income. Income up to 1000 pays 0. Income from 1001 to 5000 pays income minus 1000. Income above 5000 pays 4000 plus 3 times the amount above 5000.
tasks.sig_L: function tax(income: int) -> int
tasks.sig_py: def tax(income: int) -> int

tasks.contract: Write a function producing a greeting for a name and an hour from 0 to 23. Before 12 the greeting is Good morning, then before 18 it is Good afternoon, otherwise Good evening. The result is the greeting, a comma and space, then the name.
tasks.sig_L: function greet(name: string, hour: int) -> string
tasks.sig_py: def greet(name: str, hour: int) -> str

tasks.contract: Write a function producing one receipt line for an item name, a quantity, and a unit price. The format is the item, a space, the letter x directly followed by the quantity, a space, an equals sign, a space, and the total quantity times price.
tasks.sig_L: function line(item: string, qty: int, price: int) -> string
tasks.sig_py: def line(item: str, qty: int, price: int) -> str

tasks.contract: Write a function that formats a count of things. When n is exactly 1 the result is 1, a space, and the word. Otherwise the result is n, a space, and the word with the letter s appended.
tasks.sig_L: function plural(word: string, n: int) -> string
tasks.sig_py: def plural(word: str, n: int) -> str

tasks.contract: Write a function that returns a progress bar string of exactly n hash characters. Zero gives the empty string. n is non-negative.
tasks.sig_L: function bar(n: int) -> string
tasks.sig_py: def bar(n: int) -> str

tasks.contract: Write a function that reports the sum and maximum of a non-empty integer array as a string of the exact form sum=S max=M, using two helper functions of your own, one for the sum and one for the maximum.
tasks.sig_L: function report(xs: Array<int>) -> string
tasks.sig_py: def report(xs: list[int]) -> str

tasks.contract: Write a function that classifies a triangle from three positive integer side lengths. If the sides cannot form a triangle under the strict triangle inequality return invalid. If all sides are equal return equilateral. If exactly two sides are equal return isosceles. Otherwise return scalene. Use a helper function for the validity test.
tasks.sig_L: function triangle(a: int, b: int, c: int) -> string
tasks.sig_py: def triangle(a: int, b: int, c: int) -> str

tasks.contract: Write a function computing weekly pay from hours worked and an hourly rate. Hours up to 40 are paid at the rate. Hours above 40 are paid at double the rate. Use a helper function that returns the overtime hours.
tasks.sig_L: function pay(hours: int, rate: int) -> int
tasks.sig_py: def pay(hours: int, rate: int) -> int

tasks.contract: Write a function that totals league points from an array of result strings. A win is worth 3 points, a draw 1 point, and anything else 0 points. Use a helper function that scores a single result.
tasks.sig_L: function total(results: Array<string>) -> int
tasks.sig_py: def total(results: list[str]) -> int

tasks.contract: The given program moves a point on a grid for directions N, S, and E, leaving other directions unchanged. Extend it so that direction W decreases x by 1, keeping all existing behavior identical.
tasks.sig_L: function move(dir: string, x: int, y: int) -> { x: int, y: int }
tasks.sig_py: def move(dir: str, x: int, y: int) -> Point  (Point is a provided dataclass with int fields x, y)

tasks.contract: The given program clamps n into [lo, hi] assuming lo <= hi. Change it so that when lo is greater than hi the function returns -1 instead, keeping all other behavior identical.
tasks.sig_L: function clamp(n: int, lo: int, hi: int) -> int
tasks.sig_py: def clamp(n: int, lo: int, hi: int) -> int

tasks.contract: The given program sums the integers from 1 up to but not including n. Change it to sum from 1 up to and including n, keeping the result 0 for n below 1.
tasks.sig_L: function sumTo(n: int) -> int
tasks.sig_py: def sum_to(n: int) -> int

tasks.contract: The given program scales a rectangle record with fields w and h. Extend the record to a box with an additional integer field d for depth, scaling all three fields by k.
tasks.sig_L: function scale(b: { w: int, h: int, d: int }, k: int) -> { w: int, h: int, d: int }
tasks.sig_py: def scale(b: Box, k: int) -> Box  (Box is a provided dataclass with int fields w, h, d)
